A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be an invertible $n \times n$ matrix over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] and $\mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf b$.
Let $\mathbf A_i$ be $\mathbf A$ with column $i$ replaced by $\mathbf b$.
Then:
:$x_i = \dfrac {\map \det {\mathbf A_i} } {\map \det {\mathbf A} }$

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Determinant of Matrix|determinant]] is [[Definition:Multilinear Mapping|multilinear]] and [[Definition:Alternating Mapping|alternating]] in the columns of a matrix.

substitutions.the column in slot i: b written as a combination of the columns of A

object_map.reformulation: Expand det(A_i) by linearity in column i, and kill all terms with a repeated column.

validity_conditions: det(A) must be non-zero to divide.
Alternation is what makes the cross terms vanish.
proof_plan:
Let $\mathbf a_1, \ldots, \mathbf a_n$ be the columns of $\mathbf A$.
Then $\mathbf b = \displaystyle \sum_j x_j \mathbf a_j$.

By linearity in column $i$:
:$\displaystyle \map \det {\mathbf A_i} = \sum_j x_j \map \det {\mathbf a_1, \ldots, \mathbf a_{i - 1}, \mathbf a_j, \mathbf a_{i + 1}, \ldots, \mathbf a_n}$

For $j \ne i$, the matrix has the column $\mathbf a_j$ twice, so its determinant is $0$ by alternation.
Hence $\map \det {\mathbf A_i} = x_i \map \det {\mathbf A}$.
